story.see: Some normally dark patches of Lake Sevan brightened on 31 August and 12 September. A shore station recorded rain around the first pass and a steady overnight breeze before the second. Both can roughen water. The seasonal radar model keeps the main lake connected through those changes.
story.physics: The water-level record was 1,900.70 metres on 31 August and 1,900.58 metres on 18 October. Our time-series model estimates roughly 1,235 square kilometres for the largest water body on all ten passes. The gauge measures height. The radar map estimates where water covers the ground.
story.lband: On a calm day, smooth water usually reflects the radar away. Ripples can send more energy back and look brighter. NISAR, the NASA–ISRO radar satellite, uses long-wavelength L-band radar for these observations, which lets it collect images through clouds.
story.people: At the Gavaraget river mouth and along the Martuni shore, flat and steep stretches can move by different amounts for the same level change. Sevan also supplies irrigation water. Armenia's Water Committee reported 75.3 million cubic metres withdrawn for irrigation in the 2026 season.
